evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.20, of standing water (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “To go bad” is the passive, corrumpī: corrumpitur, it is going off. Milk or wine that turns sour acēscit (see turn sour).
Of meat, fish or fruit that smells.

phrases.latin: cernis ut ignāvum corrumpant ōtia corpus, ut capiant vitium, nī moveantur, aquae
phrases.english: you see how idleness spoils a lazy body, and how water goes bad if it doesn’t move

phrases.latin: olea ubi lēcta siet, oleum fīat continuō, nē corrumpātur
phrases.english: once the olives have been picked, the oil should be made at once, so that they don’t go bad

sources: Lewis & Short: corrumpo · Lewis & Short: putidus
